column3: CMS body edit backsyncs as an empty body
column4: Edited the body of a published Sandbox entry directly in the CMS and triggered the cms-to-github-csdocs workflow on demand. A PR opened against the correct file, matched by url, but the regenerated body was completely empty rather than reflecting the edit. Root cause confirmed live: the pull script (cms-pull-sandbox.ts) read a body field that does not exist on a docs_article entry. The real content lives in a different field, article_content, which the script never read. Entry checked: blt89df671a312338d7.

column3: Every poll run rewrites every published entry, not just the edited one
column4: The same PR from the body edit test also rewrote a second entry, Entry B, that had not been touched at all. Confirmed the sync had no diffing or filtering: it fetched every published entry from Sandbox and regenerated its file from scratch on every single run, so any published entry got its title and description mangled on every cycle whether or not a writer changed anything.

column3: Title only edit updates only the title, file path stays stable
column4: Edited only the title field on Entry A, leaving the body untouched. The resulting PR kept the same file path, since the file is matched by its url field rather than its title. Also confirmed the title came back with a product name prefix such as [Brand Kit] - that was added by the push side and was never stripped on the way back, so a plain CMS title edit still showed up polluted with that prefix in the regenerated frontmatter.

column3: SEO description and tag edits produce no visible change at all
column4: Edited the entry's SEO description field and added a tag directly in the CMS, leaving the body and title untouched. The resulting PR showed no trace of either edit anywhere in the diff. The script only ever read a flat description field that does not exist on these entries, the real SEO description lives nested one level deeper at entry.seo.description, and tags were never read at all. Entry checked: bltac9e98d0c42417c1.

column3: Whitespace only edit in the rich text editor produces the same diff as before it
column4: Round 12 re-test: added an empty paragraph, a non-breaking-space-only paragraph, and a whitespace-only paragraph inside a section that also had real content before and after, on a fresh fixture entry (blt53df765506c51e70, url /developer-resources/docops-round12-sync-retest). Ran the pull script locally against live Sandbox. All three whitespace variants produced zero visible artifacts, no stray blank lines, no leftover markers, just the real content before and after with normal single-blank-line paragraph spacing.
column5: Pass - now that scenario 1's empty-body bug is fixed
column6: whitespace-only paragraphs are correctly dropped with no artifacts

column3: Two edits before the first PR merges create two separate competing PRs
column4: Edited Entry A's body once and triggered the workflow, then, without merging that PR, edited it again and triggered the workflow a second time. Two separate branches and PRs were created, both against the same file, with no lookup of the already open PR and no reuse or update of it. A human reviewer today would have to notice and manually close or reconcile the duplicate.
column5: Noted - not addressed by the Round 9 fix

column3: Docs lint on the auto PR blocks the broken regenerated files from actually merging
column4: Both PRs from the rapid double edit test (scenario 6) failed the existing lint check, because the regenerated file was missing its required description frontmatter field, the same field that silently disappeared due to the entry.description versus entry.seo.description mismatch (scenario 4). This meant the empty body and title prefix defects were not actually reaching main, the pre-existing lint gate happened to catch the missing field and block the merge, even though that was not its intended purpose.
column5: Superseded - description now populates correctly, so this accidental protection no longer triggers on this defect

column3: Fix merged for empty body / rewrite-every-run / title prefix / SEO+tags
column4: Root cause fix for scenarios 1-4 above, all in tools/cs-sync/src/cms-pull-sandbox.ts. For csdocs: body is now built from article_content via extractSections() plus htmlToMarkdown() (matching the already-correct cms-pull.ts), a file is only written when the rebuilt content actually differs from what is on disk (fixes scenario 2), the [Marker] - title prefix is stripped via a shared parseTitle() helper moved into lib/entry-content.ts (fixes scenario 3), and description/tags are read from entry.seo.description and entry.tags respectively, filtering out the automation's own sandbox-uid-*/pr-*/nav-subsection-* tags before writing (fixes scenario 4). apidocs (api_detail_page) behavior is intentionally unchanged, its schema has not been separately verified. Merged as PR #268 (commit cd21acdf). Round 12 live re-verification: the original Round 8 fixture entries (blt89df671a312338d7, bltac9e98d0c42417c1) were no longer published in Sandbox, so a fresh fixture entry (blt53df765506c51e70, url /developer-resources/docops-round12-sync-retest) was created for this round. Body edit reflected correctly (scenario 1 confirmed fixed). A separate untouched control entry was not rewritten, and the sync log reported syncing only the one edited entry per run (scenario 2 confirmed fixed). Title-only edit kept the same file path with no leftover marker prefix (scenario 3 confirmed fixed). SEO description and tag edits came through correctly, with sandbox-uid-*/pr-*/nav-subsection-* tags correctly filtered out (scenario 4 confirmed fixed). Also ran the real cms-to-github-csdocs workflow end to end via workflow_dispatch (not just the local script), which produced PR #382 with a correct diff and a passing lint check once the fixture content itself was made lint compliant, confirming the fix works through the full PR and lint flow that Round 11 never tested. PR #382 was merged, and the test entry/file were cleaned up afterward.
column5: Fixed and live-verified end to end (local script and real GitHub Actions workflow)

column3: Add each callout type via the CMS rich text toolbar
column4:
Appended a section to fixture entry blt9371d46b757a9058 (file cs-docs/brand-kit/docops-nested-test-callout-table-code-s7.md) with

blocks, each with the toolbar's usual bold label prefix. All four converted correctly to **Note:**, **Tip:**, **Warning:**, and **Additional Resource:** paragraphs, matching the existing callout convention. Also noticed a side effect unrelated to callouts: regenerating the file downgraded the page's pre-existing top-level # H1 title line to ##, and stripped the ```text language tag off the pre-existing fenced code block down to a bare ```. column3: Add/edit a table via the CMS table editor
column4: Appended a 2-row table: one cell with a literal leading '-' character, one cell with a nested bullet list. The leading '-' cell converted correctly as plain text (not turned into a list marker). But the cell containing a nested list broke the table: the list rendered as raw list markdown with embedded newlines inside the table row, which is invalid GFM table syntax (a table row cannot contain a literal newline). The resulting row will not render as a table in that cell.
column5: Fail - nested list inside a table cell corrupts the markdown table row (embedded newlines break GFM table syntax)

column3: Add bold/italic/code/headings via the CMS editor
column4: Appended a section with <h2>/<h3> headings, <strong>, <em>, inline <code>, and a <pre> block using CS's real <br code="[object Object]"/> line-break markup (no inner <code> element, matching how Contentstack's editor actually emits pre blocks). All converted correctly: ## / ### headings, **bold**, _italic_, backtick inline code, and a properly fenced code block with real line breaks preserved.

column3: Add an image via the CMS media picker
column4: Appended a section with an tag (no src, matching CS's lazy-loaded picker output) pointing at a real Sandbox CDN asset (images.contentstack.io, asset_uid blt2455b05e4d317b26, reused from an existing entry's image). Confirms via live test what the code already showed: the pull script never downloads asset bytes into the repo. The markdown just references the CDN URL directly (![alt](https://images.contentstack.io/...)), so the GitHub file depends on the external CMS CDN rather than a committed local image.
column5: Pass (as designed) - no download/commit-to-repo behavior exists for this direction. Confirmed intentional, not a defect, but worth being aware of

column3: Add internal and external links via the CMS link tool
column4: Appended a section with an <a href="/headless-cms/create-a-branch"> internal link and an <a href="https://www.contentstack.com"> external link. Both converted correctly to [text](url) markdown, the internal link kept its relative path and the external link kept its full URL.

column3: Paste content copied from Word/Google Docs into the CMS editor
column4:
Appended a section built from typical MS Word paste markup:

wrappers, and , tags, HTML-entity smart quotes and an em dash, plus Word's fake-list markup (

with a manually numbered '1.'/'2.' prefix and mso-list:Ignore spans, rather than real

    /
  1. tags). All the mso-*/Mso* classes, inline styles, and tags were stripped cleanly, and the smart quotes/em dash survived as literal characters. However, the fake numbered list did not get recognized as a real list: it came through as two separate paragraphs whose text happens to start with '1.' and '2.', not a semantic markdown ordered list. It reads correctly here only because Word's manual numbering happened to be sequential and correct - if a writer had pasted a Word list with inconsistent/restarted numbering, or content between items, the output would carry that same mistake through as plain text.
column5: Pass with caveat - MSO markup/smart quotes handled well, but Word/Docs fake-list paragraphs are not upgraded to real markdown lists

column3: Create a brand-new entry directly in Sandbox CMS
column4: Confirmed via code research (getFilePath() in cms-pull-sandbox.ts): a brand-new entry only becomes a file if its url already matches an existing cs-docs file. There is no folder-placement logic for a url with no match. Fixing this properly would require the CMS left-nav content types (left_navigation_2026, product_navigation, links_2026) to exist and be populated in Sandbox the same way they are in Production, and nothing in the codebase confirms that is the case there. Sandbox is only in use for a couple more weeks before the repo points directly at Production, where the equivalent nav-tree logic (nav-tree.ts) already works today, so building a Sandbox-specific version would be throwaway engineering.
column5: Won't fix for Sandbox. Recommend content managers don't create brand-new docs directly in Sandbox CMS for now, add via GitHub instead. Revisit once repo points directly at Production.

column3: Unpublish/delete an entry in Sandbox CMS
column4: Fixed in cms-pull-sandbox.ts: every file the sync creates or updates now gets a uid frontmatter field stamped with the entry's CMS uid, so a file can be identified as CMS-owned. A new pass after the main sync loop compares every uid-marked file in cs-docs/ against the current set of published entries and removes any file whose entry is no longer published. Live-tested against Sandbox: created and published a fresh test entry (blt1f10ca347307f47a, url /developer-resources/docops-round11-delete-restore-test), ran the pull script locally to confirm the file was created with the uid marker, then unpublished the entry and reran the script. The file was correctly removed (git status showed the deletion), with a log line naming the entry. Only files carrying the uid marker are ever considered for deletion, so a hand-authored file that happens to share a url is never at risk.
column5: Fixed and live-verified locally. Not yet run through the real GitHub Actions workflow/PR (validated via direct script run only, per explicit choice to avoid pushing to GitHub during this test).

column4: Live-tested by republishing the same entry from scenario 19 and rerunning the pull script. The file did NOT reappear: once scenario 19's fix correctly deletes the file on unpublish, republishing hits the exact same limitation as scenario 18 (create), since the sync only ever matches an entry to a file by url, and there is no file left to match once it has been deleted. This is a real, load-bearing side effect of fixing scenario 19 correctly: previously, republishing appeared to 'restore' the file only because unpublishing never actually deleted it in the first place.
column5: Not fixed, and now behaves differently than before. Content managers should be told that unpublishing then republishing an entry in Sandbox no longer auto-restores the file. Recreating it requires the same manual step as a brand-new entry (see scenario 18) until the create-gap is addressed.

column3: Testing incident: a live Sandbox entry unrelated to this round was accidentally deleted during cleanup
column4: While cleaning up after scenario 8's re-verification, a cleanup call intended for the Round 12 test entry (blt53df765506c51e70) was mistakenly run against a different, pre-existing entry instead (blt44cad62a61cef7fe, 'Update Test2 About Assets', url /assets/test-about-assets) that had only been reused as a read-only control fixture, not created for this round. The entry was permanently deleted with no recovery path found via the Management API. A backup of its last-known content (title, url, full body) was saved from the still-intact cs-docs/docops-round12-control.md file before that file could be auto-removed by the sync's delete-pass, but the original entry itself, its uid, and its edit history are gone.
column5: Not a defect in the sync tool. Recorded as a testing-process incident. Recovery/restoration of the deleted entry is still outstanding and left for manual follow-up.
